cohort: 1000 nulliparous women from a larger cohort of 19,001 women who gave birth at a metropolitan tertiary hospital in Australia between 2011 and 2014
finding: The study found that women receiving care through a caseload midwifery program (CMP) had a significantly higher rate of normal vaginal birth compared to those receiving standard midwifery-led care (SMC).
mod_finding: Women in the CMP group had a higher rate of normal vaginal birth and lower rates of instrumental birth, episiotomy, epidural analgesia, and amniotomy.
